title: Polenta con Gorgonzola
subtitle: soft polenta with melted Gorgonzola dolce
excerpt: Polenta con Gorgonzola stirs crumbled Gorgonzola dolce into hot, buttered polenta until the cheese melts into a pungent, creamy mass. It is rich and strong in flavour: a small portion goes a long way. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Polenta with Gorgonzola is a Lombard preparation, drawing on two of the region's most important products. Gorgonzola DOP is one of Italy's oldest blue cheeses, produced in Lombardy since at least the 10th century according to the Consorzio per la Tutela del Formaggio Gorgonzola (Gorgonzola Cheese Consortium). Gorgonzola dolce, the younger, milder, creamier variety, melts into polenta more evenly than piccante. Pellegrino Artusi, La scienza in cucina (1891, public domain in Italy), gives polenta with cheese combinations as a standard Lombard preparation. Fernanda Gosetti, La cucina regionale italiana (1967, Mondadori), includes polenta con Gorgonzola as a definitive Lombard dish.

glossaryTerms.definition: The younger, creamier variety of Gorgonzola DOP. It is soft enough to melt into hot polenta without becoming grainy or stringy. Gorgonzola piccante is stronger and more crumbly; it can be used but produces a more pungent result and may not melt as smoothly.

content.text: Polenta con Gorgonzola is strong, rich, and very indulgent. Soft buttered polenta is the base;

, added off the heat and stirred until melted, is what makes it worth eating. Mild, slightly sweet polenta and pungent blue cheese is a classic Lombard balance. Neither is subtle. They work better together than apart.

Use Gorgonzola dolce if you can find it: the creamy texture melts into polenta more evenly. Gorgonzola piccante works but is more assertive and may feel overwhleming in a full bowl. This is a dish to serve in smaller portions alongside roasted vegetables or a bitter salad of radicchio.

Bring {{water}} of water to the boil. Add {{salt-table}} of salt. Whisk in {{polenta-coarse}} of polenta in a steady stream. Reduce heat to very low and cook, stirring frequently, for the time on the packet (5 minutes for instant; 35 to 40 minutes for coarse). The polenta should be thick and smooth.

Remove from the heat. Stir in {{unsalted-butter}} of cold butter until melted. Add {{gorgonzola}} of crumbled Gorgonzola dolce and stir vigorously until it melts completely into the polenta. Season with {{black-pepper}} of black pepper. Taste for salt: Gorgonzola is already salty.
Serve immediately in warm bowls. Scatter with roughly chopped walnuts if using. Serve alongside radicchio salad or roasted chicory to balance the richness.

items.symptom: Gorgonzola forms clumps rather than melting smoothly
items.cause: Cheese added when polenta is too cool, or piccante variety used
items.fix: The polenta must be very hot when cheese is added. Stir vigorously and continuously. If using piccante Gorgonzola, crumble it very finely.

items.cause: Added too much salt before the Gorgonzola, which is already very salty
items.fix: Use only 1 teaspoon of salt for the polenta. Taste and adjust only after the Gorgonzola has been incorporated.

content.text: Polenta con Gorgonzola is from the Po valley and the Lombard plains, where winter cooking runs rich and hearty. Gorgonzola takes its name from the village near Milan where it was aged in the cold November air. Polenta was the staple grain of northern Italy before rice took over in the 18th century, and it never left Lombard tables. The two together are winter comfort food in its purest form: nothing sophisticated, nothing held back.
